input.objective:
Deploy one contract, JobEightCheckDeployer, on Robinhood Chain: its constructor takes the Robinhood Chain PoolManager 0x8366a39CC670B4001A1121B8F6A443A643e40951, $owner and the fee recipient 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34, takes no salt argument, starts at salt 0 and increments until the CREATE2 address carries the hook's permission flags, then creates JobEightCheck in the launch transaction, passing the PoolManager, $owner and fee recipient unchanged to the hook constructor; neither constructor calls any other contract (apart from the deployer creating the hook). There is no deploy function to call afterwards; hook() returns the hook's address. Enable only the callbacks the behavior below needs.
JobEightCheck is a standalone Uniswap v4 hook with no new token and no pool of its own; anyone may initialize an eligible pool with it.
Only pools whose currency0 is native ETH may be initialized with this hook; any other initialization reverts.
In this hook, the token is the pool's non-ETH currency and its total supply is that token's totalSupply().
Every pool-dependent view, state, window and limit is keyed by PoolId and isolated per pool; pass the pool id to each pool-dependent function.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Take 1.0% of the ETH side of every buy and sell as a hook fee, settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34. Expose claimFees(PoolId poolId) that anyone may call to redeem that pool's claims using the same distribution. Fees are computed on the amount actually traded; when the swap specifies its ETH amount and the pool fills only part of it, the swap reverts rather than overpaying.
2. For the first 10 minutes of block timestamp after the pool's first swap, each wallet may buy at most 1.0% of the token's total supply in total; larger buys revert. Track the window and each wallet's bought total separately by PoolId. Expose windowEndsAt(PoolId poolId) as a view. A wallet means tx.origin; several wallets or a shared relayer can defeat the limit.
3. Collect 1.0% of the ETH side of every swap into a jar held by the hook, tracked separately by PoolId and settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly). When the jar holds at least 0.1 ETH, anyone may call buyback(PoolId poolId). Buy only inside buyback(), never inside a swap, from this same pool, with a price limit 3% above the pool price at the start of the call; keep any unspent ETH in that pool's jar and anyone may call it again. attempt to burn with the token's burn(uint256); if it has none, or the burn call reverts, keep them in the hook forever; no function can move retained tokens. Expose jar(PoolId poolId) as a view. Fees are computed on the amount actually traded; when the swap specifies its ETH amount and the pool fills only part of it, the swap reverts rather than overpaying.
Owner 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34 is $owner. No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the ETH (pair currency) side, never from the pool’s token; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem. Fee recipient: 0x6cba4751742f6989fa224b2dc5d5d52fcef98a34.
The hook uses no outside pool, token, price feed or service; every price it needs comes from its own pool.
Use mulDiv for every percentage calculation, including fees, shares, limits and price moves, to avoid intermediate multiplication overflow.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.
